wine.name: Soalheiro Alvarinho
wine.grapes: Alvarinho alone, the grape Spain calls Albariño across the Minho.
wine.sites: Alvarinho from the family's own vineyards and those of a circle of local growing families, mostly in the valley of Melgaço on granite, in the warm, sheltered lee of the hills above the Minho.
wine.making: After pressing, the must is clarified at a low temperature, then fermented cool in stainless steel tanks. The wine matures on its fine lees until bottling and sees no oak.
wine.glass: Ripe peach and peach skin over orange blossom, with a salty edge; dry and fresh, yet rounder and riper than a light Vinho Verde, with real weight and length.
wine.ageing: Open and fresh on release, within a year or two of the harvest; it also keeps and gains depth in bottle for several years, as the house and its importers note.
wine.serve: 8 to 10 degrees Celsius; no decanter; a white wine glass.

label.means: The grape, the Albariño of Spain across the Minho, named alone on a varietal Vinho Verde.
The sub-region of DOC Vinho Verde on the Minho, Alvarinho's home, which the bottle names beside the DOC.

records.table: Soalheiro Alvarinho is the wine a Melgaço family first bottled in its garage in 1982, by its own account the first Alvarinho brand of the municipality. Ripe peach and orange blossom over a salty edge, it is Alvarinho of Monção e Melgaço with weight and length.
records.story: In 1974 a Melgaço family planted a vineyard of Alvarinho near the town, by its own account the first continuous vineyard of the grape in the municipality. The founder, who worked in the local finance office while his wife taught at the primary school, planted it with his parents, and following the local custom of naming land the plot was called Soalheiro, a place that takes the sun. In 1982, again by the house's account, he made and bottled the first wine in the family garage, and Soalheiro became the first Alvarinho brand of Melgaço. The vineyard of 1974 gives the house its Primeiras Vinhas. The next generation of the family, an oenologist among them, later joined the house, which also draws on a circle of local growing families beside its own vines. The range widened to wines such as Granit, from high granite plots, while the plain Soalheiro Alvarinho, made in steel and kept on its fine lees, remained its core. For a sommelier it is the plain lesson in what Melgaço gives Alvarinho: ripeness, weight and length from a sheltered valley, a world away from a light, blended Vinho Verde.

others.name: Soalheiro Primeiras Vinhas
others.note: Alvarinho from the family's first vineyard, planted in 1974, fermented mostly in steel with a small part in used oak casks.

others.name: Soalheiro Granit
others.note: Alvarinho from small plots on granite at about 400 metres, fermented warmer than usual and stirred on its fine lees.

traps: The label's Monção e Melgaço is a sub-region of DOC Vinho Verde, not an appellation of its own.
Alvarinho and Albariño are one grape on two banks of the Minho; Soalheiro is Portuguese, from Melgaço, not a wine of Rías Baixas.
Monção e Melgaço is inland and sheltered, warmer and drier than the coast, not the coolest corner of Vinho Verde.

wine.name: Palácio da Brejoeira Alvarinho
wine.grapes: Alvarinho alone, from the estate's own vineyard around the palace.
wine.sites: The vineyard of the walled estate around the palace at Pinheiros, just south of the town of Monção, planted to Alvarinho from 1964.
wine.making: Made and bottled in the estate's own cellar, built in 1974. The must is fermented at a controlled low temperature in stainless steel, without oak, and the wine rests on its lees before bottling, then spends some months in bottle at the estate before it is released.
wine.glass: Pale straw; grapefruit, green apple and white peach over acacia blossom and a saline edge, with good body for a Vinho Verde, fresh acidity and a long, dry finish.
wine.ageing: Ready on release, it has the stamina to age and gains depth and complexity over several years in bottle.
wine.serve: 10 to 12 degrees Celsius; no decanter; a white wine glass.

label.means: The neoclassical palace and estate at Pinheiros, Monção, where the wine is grown, made and bottled.
The grape, named alone: the wine is Alvarinho from the estate's own vines.
The DOC of the Minho; Monção lies in its Monção e Melgaço sub-region.

records.table: Palácio da Brejoeira Alvarinho comes from the vines around a neoclassical palace near Monção, first sold under the estate's name in 1976. Pure Alvarinho, kept on its fine lees, it joins grapefruit and white peach to a saline edge and has the body to age.
records.story: The Palácio da Brejoeira stands at Pinheiros, just south of Monção: an L shaped palace of granite with three towers, built in the neoclassical style for the owner of the Brejoeira estate. Work began around the turn of the nineteenth century and was finished only about 1834. A decree of 16 June 1910 classed it a national monument. In 1937 the palace changed hands again, bought by a father as a gift for his daughter, Maria Hermínia d'Oliveira Paes (1918 to 2015). By the house's account she restructured the estate and in 1964 began planting its first Alvarinho; in 1974 she had a cellar built, and in 1976 the Palácio da Brejoeira Alvarinho was launched, bottled at the estate; other accounts give much of that work to her companion. She lived in the private part of the palace until her death on 30 December 2015. The estate also distils its Alvarinho into an old brandy aged in French oak. For a sommelier, Brejoeira is the estate Alvarinho of Monção: one grape and one estate, with a palace on the label and bottlings that go back to 1976.

others.name: Aguardente Vínica Velha Palácio da Brejoeira
others.note: An old brandy distilled from the estate's Alvarinho wine and aged for years in French oak casks in the old cellar.

traps: The palace is far older than the wine: it was classed a national monument in 1910, and its Alvarinho was first sold in 1976.
Brejoeira lies in Monção and Soalheiro in neighbouring Melgaço; both stand in the one sub-region of Monção e Melgaço.
Palácio da Brejoeira is an estate wine of a single grape, not a blended Vinho Verde of Loureiro and Trajadura.

cards.front: Palácio da Brejoeira: when was its Alvarinho first launched, and where is it bottled?

cards.front: By what act was the Palácio da Brejoeira classed a national monument, and when?

questions.q: A guest asks what grapes go into the white of the Palácio da Brejoeira. What do you answer?
questions.exp: The flagship is a varietal Alvarinho from the estate's own vines, planted from 1964; Loureiro and Trajadura make many blended Vinho Verdes elsewhere in the region.

The plan's note is answered: 1976 for the first release, 1974 for the cellar and 1964 for the first Alvarinho are on the house's História page; the purchase of 1937 is on the house's page and the Portuguese Wikipedia; the woman is named because both give her birth in 1918 and her death on 30 December 2015.

Tension between sources: the Portuguese Wikipedia says that after her bankruptcy the estate was auctioned and bought by her companion, who built the cellar and launched the wine in 1976, where the house credits her; the record tells the cellar and the launch as the house's account and names neither the companion nor her father, whose dates were not found.

The making rests on retailers' sheets (a slow, cool fermentation, the fine lees, some months in bottle) and on the house's sheet for 2009 read through search (bottled early in the next year on its fine lees); stainless steel and the absence of oak each rest on one retailer and are left out, as is the soil, which the house calls clay and limestone, a surprise in granite country.

The plan's why (the grape's name made before most growers bottled it) found no second source and is not repeated in the record; founded is empty because the palace, the vines, the cellar and the wine each have their own year. Not in WINE_PRODUCERS.

wine.name: Muros Antigos Alvarinho
wine.grapes: Alvarinho alone, from the sub-region of Monção e Melgaço.
wine.sites: Vineyards on sun facing slopes of granite in Monção e Melgaço, by the house's account among the first in the area to be picked; the range takes its name from Quinta dos Muros at Penso, where the house began.
wine.making: Picked by hand into small crates, destemmed and pressed, the must settles cold for two or three days before a long, cool fermentation in stainless steel. The wine then spends at least three months on its fine lees, stirred regularly, and sees no oak.
wine.glass: Lemon and grapefruit over wet stone; dry, taut and fresh, with more texture than a light Vinho Verde from its months on the lees, and a long, clean finish.
wine.ageing: Bright and ready on release, it also keeps: the house gives it a life of about ten years, and tastings of older vintages have shown it fresh well beyond its first few years.
wine.serve: 8 to 10 degrees Celsius; no decanter; a white wine glass.

label.means: Old walls, in Portuguese: the house's unoaked range, named, by its account, from Quinta dos Muros at Penso.
The grape, named alone on a varietal Vinho Verde, here from Monção e Melgaço.

records.table: Muros Antigos Alvarinho is the unoaked Alvarinho of Anselmo Mendes, a Melgaço house founded in 1998 by a winemaker born in Monção. Fermented cool in steel and stirred on its lees for months, it shows lemon and grapefruit with a taut, dry finish.
records.story: The house of Anselmo Mendes carries the name of its founder, an oenologist born in Monção to a farming family with vines of its own. He studied agro-industrial engineering and then oenology, and worked as an oenologist for other houses before setting out on his own. In 1998, by the house's account, he launched wines under his own signature in Monção e Melgaço and made his first Alvarinhos in a small cellar at Quinta dos Muros in Penso, Melgaço; the walled quinta gave its name to the Muros de Melgaço and Muros Antigos ranges. An order of 16 January 2001 drew the sub-regions of Vinho Verde, among them one named Monção that took in Melgaço too, and an order of 23 March 2009 renamed it Monção e Melgaço. The house became known for testing what Alvarinho can take: long ageing on the lees, fermentation and ageing in new oak barrels for Parcela Única, and Curtimenta, made with time on the skins. Muros Antigos stayed the unoaked core of the range, joined by Escolha, a blend of Alvarinho, Loureiro and Avesso. For a sommelier it is the measure of the house without wood: Alvarinho kept fresh and dry, and given texture by its lees rather than by oak.

others.name: Parcela Única

others.name: Curtimenta

others.name: Muros Antigos Escolha

Curtimenta means skin contact: it names a method used on a white grape, not a grape or a place.

The decree law 28/2001 of 16 January 2001 renaming Monção as Monção e Melgaço is from the CVRVV's own pages read through search; one secondary site dates the renaming to 1974, which the CVRVV contradicts.

wine.name: Casal Garcia
wine.grapes: A blend of Trajadura, Loureiro and Arinto with Fernão Pires, by the house's recent sheet; older accounts give Azal among its grapes.
wine.sites: Named for the vineyard at Quinta da Aveleda, Penafiel, whose grapes made the first wine in 1939; the house's sheet gives granite soils for the blend.
wine.making: The grapes are pressed gently at low pressure and the must is fermented at a controlled 16 to 18 degrees Celsius. Before bottling the wine is filtered with care and stabilised by cold; it is bottled young, medium dry and lightly effervescent, to be drunk within two or three years.
wine.glass: Pale lemon green with a light prickle; lemon zest, lime and green apple over unripe pear and white blossom, light in body and low in alcohol, with zesty acidity and a soft touch of sweetness.
wine.ageing: Made to be drunk young and fresh: the house advises drinking it within two or three years of bottling, while the prickle and the fruit are lively.
wine.serve: 8 to 10 degrees Celsius, as the house advises; no decanter; a white wine glass.

label.means: The name of the Aveleda vineyard whose grapes made the first wine, in 1939.
The DOC of the Minho, demarcated in 1908: young, fresh wine, here a blend of several white grapes.

records.table: Casal Garcia is the Vinho Verde of Aveleda, the Guedes family's house at Penafiel, first made in 1939. A blend of four white grapes, Trajadura and Loureiro among them, medium dry, low in alcohol and lightly prickling, it is poured young and well chilled.
records.story: Aveleda dates its company to 1870, when a forebear of the Guedes family built a cellar at Quinta da Aveleda in Penafiel for 300 barrels of wine, at a time when the quinta itself made only 30; the estate's first records go back to the sixteenth century. In 1908 the Vinho Verde region was demarcated by law, and Penafiel lies within its Sousa sub-region. In the late 1930s, by the house's account, a French winemaker returning by train from the Douro harvest stopped at Aveleda and fell into talk with the family's third generation. The wine they launched together in 1939 took the name of the vineyard its grapes came from: Casal Garcia. It grew into a brand of several styles, a sweeter white sold as IG Minho among them, and five generations of the family have led the company. For a sommelier, Casal Garcia is the classic picture of the light, blended, lightly prickling Vinho Verde: several white grapes, medium dry and low in alcohol, made to be drunk young. It is the style against which the single grape wines of Monção e Melgaço and the Lima are measured.

others.name: Casal Garcia Sweet White
others.note: A sweeter white of the same grapes, low in alcohol and sold as IG Minho rather than DOC Vinho Verde.

traps: Casal Garcia is the brand; Aveleda is the house that makes it, at Quinta da Aveleda in Penafiel, in the Sousa sub-region.
Casal Garcia Sweet White is an IG Minho wine, not DOC Vinho Verde like the white.
Its light prickle is part of the style of a young, blended Vinho Verde; it is not a sparkling wine.

cards.front: Casal Garcia: where does the wine's name come from?

The plan's note is answered in part: 1939 is on the house's timeline and its brand page and on importers' pages; the blend on the house's current white sheet is Trajadura, Loureiro, Arinto and Fernão Pires, not Azal, so the record gives the sheet's four and says older accounts name Azal (the plan's report and several retailers).

The French winemaker's visit is 1937 on the house's timeline and 1936 on its Casal Garcia brand page, so the story says the late 1930s; he and the third generation owner are described, not named, for want of their dates; the founder of 1870 is described as a forebear of the family for the same reason.

The house's sheet calls the wine medium dry and lightly effervescent; how the prickle is made (added carbon dioxide or not) was not found in any source, so the record does not say; the lace of the label and the story told of it (a lace cloth wiping a dusty bottle) rest on a retailer and Vivino only and are left out.

Left out as volatile or a ranking: the claims that Casal Garcia is the best selling Vinho Verde in the world and present in some seventy countries; the 1910 union of the estate, on which the house's pages disagree (an uncle's half or a brother's share).
Penafiel in the Sousa sub-region is on the CVRVV's own page, which agrees with the region record's producers line. Not in WINE_PRODUCERS.
Living people met and not named: the family's fourth and fifth generations who lead the company.

wine.name: Ameal Loureiro
wine.grapes: Loureiro alone, the white grape of the Lima valley.
wine.sites: The estate's own Loureiro vineyards beside some 800 metres of the river Lima's bank at Refóios do Lima, about 30 kilometres from the Atlantic, on soils of granitic origin.
wine.making: Picked by hand and pressed whole in a pneumatic press, the must settles cold for a day or two, then ferments for twelve to fifteen days at a controlled 16 to 18 degrees Celsius in stainless steel. The wine then rests on its fine lees in steel for about seven months before bottling.
wine.glass: Bright citrine; orange blossom and the floral scent Loureiro is known for, light to medium in body, vibrant and dry, with refreshing acidity and a clean, lively finish.
wine.ageing: Fresh and vibrant on release; its acidity, the house says, promises good evolution in bottle over a few years, while the oak aged Reserva is the estate's wine for longer keeping.
wine.serve: 8 to 10 degrees Celsius; no decanter; a white wine glass.

label.means: Quinta do Ameal, the estate on the Lima whose own Loureiro fills the bottle.
The grape, named alone: the Lima sub-region's white wines of note are made from it.
The DOC of the Minho; the estate lies in its Lima sub-region.

records.table: Ameal Loureiro comes from Quinta do Ameal on the river Lima, an estate with records from 1710. Pure Loureiro, fermented in steel and kept some seven months on its fine lees, it is bright, dry and scented with orange blossom.
records.story: Quinta do Ameal lies along the bank of the Lima at Refóios do Lima, by Ponte de Lima, and its records go back to 1710. In the 1990s the estate passed to a family that set out to show what Loureiro, the Lima valley's own white grape, could do alone, and by the house's own account Ameal became a pioneer of Loureiro bottled as a single grape. In 2000 the estate made its first trials of Loureiro aged in French oak barrels, the beginning of the wine first called Escolha and later Reserva, which comes from its Marinhas plot. In 2019 the estate was sold to Esporão, the Alentejo house, which kept its work on Loureiro, and the wines came to carry the name Ameal on their labels. The flagship stayed what it had been: Loureiro alone from the estate, fermented in steel and kept on its fine lees for months. For a sommelier, Ameal Loureiro is the lesson in the Lima's grape, made with the care Monção e Melgaço gives Alvarinho, and the proof that a serious Vinho Verde can rest on a single grape other than Alvarinho.

others.name: Ameal Reserva
others.note: Loureiro from the Marinhas plot, aged in oak; known as Escolha until it took its present name, its line began with trials in French oak in 2000.

traps: Loureiro, not Alvarinho, is the grape of the Lima valley; Ameal Loureiro is a varietal of the Lima sub-region, not of Monção e Melgaço.
Ameal Reserva is the oak aged Loureiro, formerly Escolha; Ameal Loureiro itself is made in steel without oak.
Quinta do Ameal's records go back to 1710, but its Loureiro made the estate's name only from the 1990s.

cards.front: Ameal Loureiro: how long does it rest on its fine lees, and in what?
cards.back: About seven months, in stainless steel, after a cool fermentation of twelve to fifteen days.

cards.front: Which Quinta do Ameal wine began with trials in French oak in 2000, and what was it first called?
cards.back: Ameal Reserva, from the Marinhas plot, first known as Escolha.

questions.q: A guest orders the Quinta do Ameal white and asks which sub-region of Vinho Verde it comes from. What do you answer?
questions.exp: Quinta do Ameal lies on the river Lima at Refóios do Lima, by Ponte de Lima, in the Lima sub-region, Loureiro's home; Monção e Melgaço, on the Minho, is Alvarinho's.

questions.q: Quinta do Ameal's records go back to 1710. In which year was the estate bought by Esporão, the Alentejo house?
questions.exp: Esporão bought the estate in 2019; 2000 is the year of its first trials of Loureiro in French oak, the root of the Reserva.

The plan's note is answered in part: the estate's records from 1710, its place at Refóios do Lima and its claim as a pioneer of Loureiro are Esporão's own; the sale to Esporão in 2019 is in Harpers and Wine Industry Advisor (September 2019 in one account, October in another, so the record gives the year); the label is Ameal on Esporão's sheets, while retailers still print Quinta do Ameal Loureiro for the 2019, so the record makes no claim for the year of the change.

The estate's history before 2019 is thin and conflicting: the family is said to have held it from the 1990s (Wine Industry Advisor and an importer), its planting completed in 1990 or its vineyard planted in 1948 (one source each), its first Loureiro bottled in 1999 (a blog and an importer), so the story says only the 1990s; the former owner is living and is never named, and his family's tie to a Port house rests on one source and is left out.

The Reserva of the Marinhas plot, formerly Escolha and begun with trials in French oak in 2000, is on Esporão's own Reserva page; Solo Único, from another single plot, is left out of others for want of space in the sources.

The glass follows Esporão's own sheets (bright citrine, citrus and the floral aromas typical of Loureiro, orange blossom, a vibrant palate with refreshing acidity); a retailer names lime zest, lemon and white peach, not cited for want of room among the sources, so the glass names orange blossom alone. The name Loureiro is said to come from laurel, on secondary pages only, so the record does not say it.
Founded is empty: 1710 is the first record of the estate, not a founding. The organic conversion (2005 in one account, begun plot by plot in Esporão's) is left out. Not in WINE_PRODUCERS.
Living people met and not named: the former owner, his father, Esporão's founder and the estate's winemaker.

changed: story: a pioneer in showing that the grape could make white wine of real quality on its own, with on its own said twice, now a pioneer of Loureiro bottled as a single grape, the house's claim hedged.
story: which bottles its wines under the name Ameal now the wines came to carry the name Ameal on their labels, a present habit told as history.
open: The father's purchase in 1990 (Blue Travel) and the first Loureiro of 1999 (Público) are each on one source; the story says the 1990s.
About 30 kilometres from the Atlantic rests on Esporão's page as the author read it; the refuter found the 800 metres of riverbank on Esporão's own sheet but not the distance.
